title: Grateful Dead Live at Catholic Youth Center on 1971-04-13

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality soundboard capture of a mythic show highlighted by an epic 20‑minute Good Lovin’ and fiery drumming from Bill Kreutzmann.
ai_review.review: The recording, sourced from the venue’s soundboard, generally delivers clear audio with only occasional distortion complaints. Musically the concert is remembered for its extended Good Lovin’, strong Pig Pen organ work, a memorable Me & Bobby McGee cover, and especially the “sick/chills/heavy” drum performance by Bill Kreutzmann.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews are mostly positive about the performance (high energy, standout jams) but one reviewer cites serious distortion, leading to a balanced overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Several reviewers praise the good‑quality soundboard source; however, one notes noticeable distortion and bad sound quality in parts of the set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Mix of extended jams (20‑minute Good Lovin’) and classic covers, with a strong second set that many listeners recall as a rare treat.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s steel guitar work during the New Riders set and his warm presence backstage are highlighted; no specific guitar tone comments for the Dead portion.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig Pen (organ) praised as being in good form; Uncle John's Band vocals noted positively.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as “sick/chills/heavy” and a major highlight of the show.
